The foundational operators—retentivity, sign-gestalt expectations, and second-order drives—are structured as a triadic hierarchy. Retentivity encodes temporal coherence in memory, enabling stable representation of past experiences. Sign-gestalt expectations act as predictive kernels that map current sensory input to anticipated outcomes, forming the basis of cognitive anticipation. Second-order drives introduce meta-level regulation, where higher-order goals influence lower-order motivational states. These primitives interact through feedback loops: retentivity sustains expectation signatures, which in turn shape second-order drives. The system exhibits dualities such as internal vs external stimuli, and linear vs non-linear response regimes. Failure modes arise when retentivity collapses (memory loss), expectations become degenerate (predictive failure), or second-order regulation breaks down (maladaptive behavior). This framework supports both Bayesian inference in GSI and dynamic state transitions in GSE.
